It is denied by default. `authorityOf` in `apps/api/src/oversight/toolAuthority.ts` treats a tool with no row as `requires_human_action`, so the tool never executes. Both enforcement points apply this. The lookup only matches the table's own keys, so an inherited name such as `toString` is denied too.

The gate (`withHumanOversight`) never calls the executor of a `requires_human_action` tool. It returns a constant result, `{"error":"requires_human_action","escalation":"blocked_consequential_call"}`, as a normal result and does not throw.

The spec also says that `assertAllToolsDeclared.ts` makes the api fail at startup if a registered tool has no declared authority. This is a spec requirement (FR-004). I did not check the implementation, only the spec text.

judgements.reason: The answer correctly describes call-time deny-by-default as requires_human_action. It only hedges on the startup refusal by assertAllToolsDeclared, citing the spec without confirming the behaviour, and it omits the conflict with docs/human-oversight.md.
